1.note: The **seventh month** of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of September and the first part of October on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

The text uses a cardinal number, **one**, to refer to the first day of the month. If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **one**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [on the first of the month]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an assembly dedicated to Yahweh]

Here and throughout the chapter, the word **you** is plural because Yahweh is telling Moses what to the say to all the Israelites. So, use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The phrase **work of service** expresses a single idea. The word **service** tells more about **work**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

The implication is that the people would blow trumpets on this day. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a day when you sound the trumpets]

2.note: Yahweh is using **a scent of pleasing** as a common expression of the culture to mean “an offering that he accepts.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as a sacrifice that is acceptable]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [to me]

It might seem that the expression **one bull, a son of cattle** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [one young bull]

Yahweh is using **sons of a year** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that are a year old]

This could mean: (1) that all the animals were **perfect**. Alternate translation: [and all the animals must be perfect] (2) that the **lambs** were **perfect**. Alternate translation: [each lamb perfect]

3.note: The expression **mixed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [flour that you have mixed with the oil]
The fraction **three tenths** means three parts out of ten equal parts.

The term **tenths** here refers to tenths of an ephah. An ephah was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

4.q: וְ⁠עִשָּׂר֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לַ⁠כֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָ⁠אֶחָ֑ד לְ⁠שִׁבְעַ֖ת הַ⁠כְּבָשִֽׂים
4.note: The implication is that one tenth of an ephah of flour is required for each one of the seven lambs. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and one tenth of an ephah of flour for each one of the seven male lambs]

5.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **buck** that is characterized by being one of the **goats**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and one male goat]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

6.note: The implication is that **the burnt offering of the month** is the offering that Yahweh required at the beginning of every month, as described in 28:11–15. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the burnt offering required at the beginning of each month]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **continuity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the burnt offering that is offered continually]

Here, the pronoun **their** could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the first day of the seventh month, the regular offering for the first day of any month, and the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings] (2) just the regular offering for the first day of any month and the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the first day of the month and the burnt offering of the continuity] (3) just the burnt offerings for the first day of the seventh month. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the first day of the seventh month]

7.note: Yahweh is using **you shall humble your souls** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall deny yourselves food and comfort.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you shall deny yourselves food and comfort]

11.note: The implication is that **the sin offering of the atonement** is the offering that Yahweh required on this one day of the year, the Day of Atonement. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the sin offering presented on this annual Day of Atonement]

Here, the pronoun **their** could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement offering, and the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings] (2) just the offering for the Day of Atonement and the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the Day of Atonement and the burnt offering of the continuity] (3) just the burnt offerings for the tenth day of the seventh month. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the tenth day of the seventh month]

17.q: וּ⁠בַ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠שֵּׁנִ֗י פָּרִ֧ים בְּנֵי־בָקָ֛ר שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר
17.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And on the second day you shall present 12 bulls, sons of cattle]

18.note: The implication is that the amounts of grain and drink offerings for each animal are the amounts that Yahweh prescribed earlier, in 29:14–15. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by their number according to the amounts prescribed earlier]

19.note: Here, the pronoun **their** could refer to: (1) the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and its drink offering] (2) the special offerings for the second day of the festival as well as the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings for the second day of the festival and for the burnt offering of the continuity]

35.note: A **holiday** is a kind of solemn gathering that closes a festival, on which people assemble to worship and do no work. If your readers would not be familiar with what a holiday is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a solemn closing assembly]

39.note: The pronoun **These** refers to all of the offerings that Yahweh has described in this chapter and the previous one. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These offerings that I have described you shall do]

This could mean: (1) that the offerings outlined in Numbers 28–29 are in addition to all these offerings. Alternate translation: [besides your burnt offerings, and besides your grain offerings, and besides your drink offerings, and besides your peace offerings] (2) that the offerings in Numbers 28–29 are these kinds of offerings. Alternate translation: [as your burnt offerings, and as your grain offerings, and as your drinking offerings, and as your peace offerings]

This is the end of the second-level quotation that began in 28:3, and it is also the end of the first-level quotation that began in 28:2. You may wish to mark the ends of these speeches with closing second-level and first-level quotation marks or with some other punctuation or convention that your language uses to indicate the end of a quotation within a quotation.
